skill.name: python-scripting
skill.description: Python scripting with uv and PEP 723 inline dependencies. Use when creating standalone Python scripts with automatic dependency management.
skill.summary: Create standalone Python scripts with uv-managed PEP 723 dependencies.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

content.value_statement: Standalone Python scripts often need repeatable dependencies and clear command-line behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to build uv scripts with PEP 723 metadata.
actual_capabilities: Creates standalone Python script plans using uv and PEP 723 metadata.
Adds inline dependency declarations for scripts that need packages.
Uses argparse patterns for input paths, output paths, and verbose mode.
Documents uv run usage and help examples for generated scripts.
Encourages reproducible dependency resolution with exclude-newer metadata.
limitations: Generated scripts still need review before execution on local files.
It does not audit third-party package security or license terms.
The template assumes uv and Python 3.12 or newer are available.
Complex applications may need packaging, tests, or project structure beyond one script.

use_cases.title: Build a File Processing Utility
use_cases.description: Create a single Python script that accepts an input file and writes processed output.

use_cases.title: Automate a Repeated Operations Task
use_cases.description: Turn a manual command-line workflow into a focused script with clear arguments.

use_cases.title: Prototype Data Cleanup
use_cases.description: Draft a small script with declared dependencies for quick data transformation work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Script
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple utility.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone Python script using uv and PEP 723 metadata. It should read one input file and print a short summary.

prompt_templates.title: Add Command-Line Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a uv Python script with argparse options for input, output, and verbose mode. Include helpful usage text.

prompt_templates.title: Use External Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone Python script with PEP 723 dependencies for requests and rich. Pin reproducibility with exclude-newer metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production-Ready Utility
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for robust scripting standards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a uv-run Python CLI utility with argument validation, clear exit codes, logging, and examples for normal and error cases.

output_examples.input: A request to create a script that summarizes a text file.
output_examples.output: A standalone script outline with uv metadata, argument parsing, file reading, summary output, and run instructions.

output_examples.input: A request to automate an API export with dependencies.
output_examples.output: A script plan that declares required packages, accepts credentials through arguments or environment configuration, and writes a chosen output file.

output_examples.input: A request to clean a CSV file from the command line.
output_examples.output: A focused CLI script structure with input and output paths, validation steps, progress messages, and reproducible dependency settings.

best_practices: Review generated dependencies and script behavior before running the script.
Keep each script focused on one task with clear inputs and outputs.
Use reproducibility metadata when scripts depend on external packages.
anti_patterns: Do not use the template for large applications that need a full package layout.
Do not run generated scripts on sensitive files without reviewing file operations.
Do not leave placeholder dependency names or script descriptions in final output.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create standalone Python scripts that use uv and PEP 723 inline dependency metadata.

faq.question: Does the skill run scripts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates for scripts that users can review and run themselves.

faq.question: Which Python version does the template expect?
faq.answer: The included template expects Python 3.12 or newer.

faq.question: Can it include third-party packages?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to declare script dependencies in PEP 723 metadata for uv.

faq.question: Is it suitable for reusable Python packages?
faq.answer: It is best for standalone scripts. Reusable packages usually need a project layout and package metadata.

faq.question: What should users check before running output?
faq.answer: Users should review dependencies, file access, network behavior, and command-line arguments before execution.
